item.title: How does Texas plan to stay focused after win over Mississippi? Try Kobe Bryant's Mamba mentality
item.description: Texas quarterback Arch Manning has been watching HBO's "Entourage" to get a laugh and cope with college football's pressure. (Jay Janner/Austin American-Statesman) AUSTIN - Texas has gone Hollywood. That's right. And we're not just talking about Arch Manning's national commercials . After two losses in the last three games but a scintillating, season-saving win over seventh-ranked Ole Miss last Saturday , the now 11th-ranked Longhorns turned to an unusual source for motivation for their final five games, starting with a home game against Mississippi State on Saturday night. Steve Sarkisian has looked to the late Kobe Bryant, the Los Angeles Lakers legend and five-time NBA champion. Sarkisian met Bryant several times because their daughters attended the same high school and played on the same volleyball team. MAILBAG: What's up with onsides kicks? He was particularly impressed with the way Bryant coached his daughter Gigi's basketball team and "watched him coach 6-year-old girls like it was the NBA Finals." "Now is not the time for a relief syndrome. Now is the time for a Mamba mentality," the Texas head coach said, channeling the Black Mamba's obsession with focus and winning and refusal to quit. "We definitely buy into that mentality. And nobody did it better than Kobe." Manning also looked to an L.A. star, albeit one off the court: television star Jeremy Piven, who played Ari Gold, the volatile, powerful agent for an A-list movie star on the hugely popular HBO series "Entourage." Yeah, Arch understands A-list. Does he ever. The Texas quarterback has watched all eight seasons of the comedy-drama, started rewatching the series and even went to one of Piven's stand-up comedy shows last offseason with some of his teammates. "He was hilarious," Manning said. "He's cool. He's probably my favorite character in all of television, Ari Gold. We've kept up on the phone. I've been able to pick his brain, and just being able to laugh is refreshing." Considering his much-scrutinized, oft-critiqued journey , laughter's a pretty good tonic for him. He clarified that he didn't so much pick the actor's brain as have good conversations and reflect on his own struggles last season. Manning told Piven he had started watching "Entourage" again, and "then we kind of got on a hot streak. He loved that." Manning was uncharacteristically at ease Monday after engineering the win. He said his roommates, like Bryce Chambers, constantly bust his chops to keep him grounded. He joked about Halloween costumes. He endorsed an East Austin pizza place. He spoke for a team that's definitely looking inward for the mental resolve needed to avoid complacency after four highly emotional football games that all came down to the final play. item.title: Dana White eats crow, apologizes to Farid Basharat for ‘turning down fights’ comments – ‘I didn’t mean to do that’
item.description: My bad, kid. Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) CEO Dana White has apologized to Farid Basharat after his comments regarding the undefeated Bantamweight’s surprising departure from the promotion painted him as potentially difficult to work with. Basharat recently fought out his UFC contract and was not offered a new deal despite winning all seven of his Octagon appearances and holding a spot in the Bantamweight rankings. When White was initially asked to explain the decision, he suggested that fighters occasionally aren’t re-signed because they turn down matchups or create problems for UFC matchmakers. “When guys’ contracts are up — and this isn’t the first time this has happened — either guys aren’t good to deal with, or the matchmakers don’t want to deal with them, which could be turning down fights or whatever the reasoning is,” White said following UFC Edmonton. “If you’re 16-0 with seven wins in the UFC and don’t get re-signed, there’s definitely a reason .” Basharat vehemently denied ever declining a fight and accused White of potentially damaging his reputation with other promotions. “Ferocious” pointed toward the injuries and extreme weight discrepancies he accepted during his UFC tenure as proof that he was never difficult to work with. During the UFC 333 post-fight press conference , White admitted his vague response unfairly placed Basharat under suspicion. “When I was talking to the media that night, and I was saying reasons that you could not get re-signed, I wasn’t saying that about him,” White explained. “I said, ‘Well, it’s happened before.’ There are lots of reasons why guys don’t get re-signed. I wasn’t talking about him specifically. “I actually saw his response video on my Instagram, and I was like, ‘Oh s—t. I didn’t mean to do that to that kid,’” White continued. “And I saw he had said something like, ‘If you’re not going to re-sign me, don’t try to hurt my career.’ And in no way, shape or form did I try to do that.” White insisted there are no personal or professional issues between UFC and Basharat, predicting that the undefeated 29-year-old will have no trouble finding another promotional home. “I have no problems with him whatsoever, personally or professionally, and I’m sure with his record and what he’s got going on, he’ll get signed somewhere,” White said. Could Basharat eventually return to the Octagon? “I wouldn’t say in the near future,” White said. “We just let him go. But I’m not saying it’s not a possibility that he could come back to the UFC.” White’s apology clears Basharat of the accusations surrounding his exit. However, it still leaves the biggest question unanswered: Why did UFC allow an undefeated, ranked contender to walk away in the first place? Well, we know the answer— less boring, more violence . item.title: Stephen A. Smith scolds Nikola Jokic for saying booing fans ‘not welcome’
item.description: Credit: Christopher Hanewinckel - Imagn Images; Stephen A. Smith on YouTube The Denver Nuggets are projected to take a step back this season, and Nikola Jokic took an unusual step in the first week by going toe-to-toe with fans who booed the team at Ball Arena. After Jokic posted a 35-point triple-double as Denver returned to beat the New Orleans Pelicans in overtime on Saturday night, the Serbian superstar said those who booed were “ not welcome ” as fans. Jokic’s stark comments came as he awaits a massive contract extension next summer and the team tries to return to the NBA Finals after a 2023 title. Among the many critics of Jokic’s surprising quip was Stephen A. Smith, who offered familiar criticism of the Nuggets star on his radio show Monday. “If ownership for the Denver Nuggets are having a heart attack from what they just heard, please forgive them,” he said. “Because that is one of the most ridiculous things you could ever want to hear from any player, let alone a superstar.” “Fans have a right to boo you. And the bigger point is, even though they booed, you know what else they did, Nikola Jokic? They stayed. So they booed you, probably to inspire you to come back and do what the hell you did. As long as they didn’t leave, why are you tripping?” Smith has repeatedly said he sees his job as making his bosses more money. And he believes Jokic would do well to embrace the same mentality. “Nikola Jokic seems to be a really great guy. He’s a great superstar for the game,” he said. “But you still can’t say that. You can’t say that. Not unless you’re playing for free. If you are getting paid, and this brother is in position to get a $300 million-plus extension. If you are getting paid, you cannot say stuff like that. You cannot disregard the importance of generating revenue. ‘Oh, there goes Stephen A. again … talking about money.’ Shut up.” Smith also contrasted Jokic’s defensive posture with LeBron James’s over the weekend, who said Philadelphia fans were right to boo the 76ers after their loss to Detroit. While Smith’s take seems in line with most Nuggets fans’ perspective, it is worth remembering that Jokic hails from a part of the world far more loyal to its sports teams. Countless viral videos have captured the incredible crowds for Serbian basketball. It would take far more than a mid-game deficit to draw boos from those fans. Also, to be fair to Jokic, the Nuggets have been decimated by failed transactions since their championship run. The team’s struggles are almost never his fault or that of the team’s core players. Still, fans have to voice their frustration somehow — even if it is toward the front office or ownership. Arsenal travel to the League Two side having lost last season’s final to Manchester City, with Arteta keen to manage his players’ workload as they compete on multiple fronts. The Spaniard made some surprise changes for the weekend victory over Everton and is expected to shuffle his pack again at Highbury Stadium, with Viktor Gyokeres and teenage prospect Max Dowman among those in contention to start. Arteta refused to underestimate the challenge posed by Fleetwood, insisting his players must understand the responsibility that comes with wearing the Arsenal shirt. “Show them the Arsenal shirt and what we represent and that’s it,” he said. “We need to go there and win the game. That’s it. It’s very simple. “Our reputation, our pride, everything is in play. So every time you play a football match, and especially against a team in a different division, respect the game, respect every opponent because they deserve to do that. item.title: Walkinshaw TWG Was Fined and Docked Points Over Fuel Paperwork. Mostert Kept the Podium Anyway.
item.description: Chaz Mostert and Fabian Coulthard's #1 Toyota GR Supra en route to victory in the AirTouch 500 at The Bend. Photo: Toyota Australia. Walkinshaw TWG Racing was fined and lost teams’ championship points after the Gold Coast 500 finale. Chaz Mostert’s podium, earned on the road, stayed exactly where it was. If that looks like a mismatch, it is, and it is deliberate: the penalty is for a paperwork-style breach, not for anything that changed the race. What the rule actually asks The investigation first appeared to be about the Mostert car’s fuel hose still being attached as the car was dropped to the ground. The breach that was cited concerned something else. A note in the pre-event authorised representatives’ briefing requires teams to tell Supercars the litres of fuel transferred in each pit stop, by direct message on the Supercars Teams App, within five laps of the stop. Walkinshaw TWG was found in breach of the pit stop refuelling requirement. The size of the fine and the number of points were not stated in the series’ own report, and Motorsport Australia had not yet published its findings when that report appeared. Treat both figures as pending. Why a litres log matters The note does not explain its own purpose, so this part is analysis. A running record of litres per stop is the sort of data a series needs if it wants to test a team’s fuel-to-finish claims after the fact. The same weekend supplied a live example: two Chevrolet teams explained late stops as fuel miscalculations, and anyone assessing those explanations wants transferred volumes, not just the story. Our coverage of those late stops and the Finals fallout covers that side. It also explains why the penalty lands on the team rather than the result. Mostert finished third, his fourth straight podium at Surfers Paradise. A reporting failure does not make a car faster, so the sanction hits the budget and the teams’ table instead. The practical damage The points deduction dropped Walkinshaw TWG behind Tickford Racing into third in the teams’ championship ahead of the Penrite Oil Sandown 500. Mostert still goes into the Semi Final starting fourth, having qualified with a dominant Saturday win. The team also used a mid-race swap to help teammate Ryan Wood chase a Finals place, a move the regulations permit that ultimately did not pay off. The Supercars field in action. Photo by Telmo Antunes via Pexels (free to use) For more on the car Mostert drives, see our look at Toyota’s GR Supra season . Our earlier piece on Gold Coast qualifying moving to Friday shows how the weekend was restructured. Sandown’s running starts Friday, November 6. item.description: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy after a rookie minicamp practice on May 9, 2026. -- Ed Thompson / Steelers Now A former NFL scout has high expectations for the Pittsburgh Steelers this season. The Pittsburgh Steelers have been playing some very good, complementary football as of late, setting themselves up to contend for the playoffs once again this year. However, former NFL scout John Middlekauf is already confident the Steelers will be in the postseason come January. “Let’s face it. At 5-2, unless they get a couple major injuries, they kind of feel like a playoff lock,” Middlekauf said on The Colin Cowherd Podcast . “Back-to-back years, keeping the Steelers in the playoffs, that’s really commendable. And the way they play, you never know, you could win a playoff game.” It is certainly a bold prediction as the Steelers are in the midst of a very tight race in the AFC North. Pittsburgh currently sits in second place behind the 5-2 Cleveland Browns and in front of the 4-2 Cincinnati Bengals and 4-3 Baltimore Ravens. Of course, teams can still make the playoffs without winning their division, but that is the easiest way to guarantee a spot in the playoffs. Middlekauf believes quarterback Aaron Rodgers will be the difference that propels the Steelers into the postseason, though. “I have so much respect for the way Aaron’s battled these last two years. item.title: Another U.S. pro sports league partners with prediction markets
item.description: Utah Jazz center Jaxson Hayes (11) dunks the ball during a game against the Los Angeles Lakers at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News The NBA announced deals Monday with two popular prediction market platforms, leaving the NFL the only major professional sports league in the U.S. not to wade into the controversial industry. The agreements with Kalshi and Polymarket are designed to establish a comprehensive framework for NBA-related prediction markets, including a memorandum of understanding with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, which regulates prediction markets in the U.S. According to the NBA, the agreements include integrity protections for NBA-related markets, including limitations on permissible markets, affirmative prohibitions on trading NBA event contracts by league and team personnel, and information-sharing obligations relating to investigations and suspicious trading. Players and league and team employees will not be allowed to trade on NBA event contracts. “Protecting the integrity of the game is our top priority,” Scott Kaufman-Ross, NBA head of media distribution and partnerships, said in a press release . “As this category develops, we believe it is important to work constructively with regulators and operators to help ensure that appropriate safeguards are in place. These partnerships represent an important step in establishing a framework that creates new opportunities to engage our fans.” Adam Barrick, Kalshi head of sports partnerships, called the partnership with the NBA a “significant milestone.” Los Angeles Lakers guard Luka Dončić (77) shoots a 3-pointer during a game against the Utah Jazz at the Delta Center in Salt Lake City on Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. | Lukas Katilius, Deseret News “The NBA is one of the most influential sports leagues in the world, and we’re excited to work together to bring fans closer to the game,” said Ari Borod, president of sports business development at Polymarket. While this is the league’s first entry into the prediction markets, individual players are already in business with companies in the industry. Front Office Sports reported that Miami Heat center Giannis Antetokounmpo is an investor in Kalshi, while new Philadelphia 76er LeBron James recently reached an endorsement deal with Polymarket that will pay him $15 million a year. San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said he would never promote a sports betting site, saying it’s “very sad” to see players do it. item.description: Lamine Yamal insists award he won at Ballon d'Or ceremony should have gone to team-mate originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Lamine Yamal may not have won the big award at the 2026 Ballon d'Or award ceremony in London on Monday night, but he was still brought up to the podium to accept a different trophy. The 19-year-old sensation won his third straight Kopa Trophy, also known as the Men's Best Young Player award. While he was believed to be amongst the favorites to win the Ballon d'Or itself that year, the Kopa Trophy was a signal that his exploits were worthy of recognition no matter how the vote played out later on. Only those 21 years old and younger are eligible to win the trophy, but the same player can win it multiple times before they are no longer of an eligible age. However, when the Barcelona sensation went up on stage to accept his trophy, he expressed his disappointment that someone different wasn't up at that podium to accept the award. MORE: A full overview of the 2026 Ballon d'Or award ceremony, including all results Lamine Yamal says Kopa Trophy should have gone to Pau Cubarsi When accepting his third Kopa Trophy for the best young player, Lamine Yamal made it clear that he felt someone else deserved the award. His teammate, fellow 19-year-old La Masia graduate Pau Cubarsi, was also nominated for the Kopa Trophy this year, but did not win. According to Lamine, he felt that the young defender should have been up there at the podium instead. "I would have liked to see my teammate [Pau] Cubarsi here because I think this prize should have been for him. He has been playing at an excellent level for some time. This is my third year up here for this prize. I would like to thank my club and my national team. "Speaking about this one specifically, this one should have been for Cubarsi." Why didn't Pau Cubarsi win the Kopa Trophy? At the end of the day, while Cubarsi did absolutely have an unbelievable season, there was no beating Lamine Yamal for the Kopa Trophy. Lamine was truly sensational for Barcelona, doing just about everything for Barcelona — not just goal scoring, but also creativity, ball progression, dribbling, and much more. Cubarsi has been a rock at the back for Barcelona for a while now, but playing in a high line under Hansi Flick, the defensive numbers they put up at the Camp Nou didn't stack up to the best defenses in the world, and thus it wasn't quite enough. Even as Cubarsi played every minute for Spain at the World Cup, Lamine being his international teammate and also winning the FIFA title meant there was no way to separate them in this way.

item.title: Brewers Already Seem Destined To Trade Brice Turang
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers second baseman Brice Turang For years, the Milwaukee Brewers have operated with a strict formula when it comes to free agency, trades and extensions. They know that if a star player plays for them and hits free agency, they are unlikely to be able to retain them. That has resulted in them trading players a year before they hit the open market, signing young players to lengthy extensions before they prove themselves and even, in rare instances, simply letting great players walk for no return. Corbin Burnes, Josh Hader, Devin Williams and Freddy Peralta were all traded before hitting the open market. Cooper Pratt, Luis Lara and Jackson Chourio were recipients of long extensions before ever playing in a big league game. Willy Adames reportedly did not even receive an offer in free agency. Knowing how the Brewers operate, the star to keep an eye on is Brice Turang. Unlike other young stars in the organization, he has not signed an extension, and his rise to stardom has priced him out of Milwaukee. He was Team USA's starting second baseman and is arguably the best second baseman in baseball. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! He has won a Platinum Glove and hit 21 home runs this year. It's a shock he has not made an All-Star Game, and the reality is that if he were playing in Los Angeles or New York, he would have. The Brewers may have more financial flexibility after their World Series run, and perhaps more incentive to keep their core of stars together. However, they likely won't change the formula that allows them to compete year in and year out. On top of that, Turang's replacement won't be hard to find. The top prospect in baseball, Jesús Made, could debut as soon as next year, and is an extension candidate already, like Chourio was. Made is a shortstop, just like Turang was, but he could easily move to second base. If the Brewers like him at shortstop long-term, Pratt could move to second. If the Brewers want to hold on to Turang until the very last moment before trading him, Made can play third base. Luis Peña and Andrew Fischer are also top prospects in the organization and will need spots to play if they are as good as the team projects they will be. In reality, the Brewers probably should have inked Turang to an extension earlier, but his first year in the big leagues was not great. His second year was better, and that should have been when the Brewers pulled the trigger, knowing that his ascension was not about to stop. Over the last two seasons, he has quickly turned into a name all baseball fans know, and soon, he could be the center of many trade rumors. More MLB: Rays Leaving Hottest Hitter Out Of Game 3 Lineup

item.title: World Series Game 3 pitching matchup features Freddy Peralta vs. Robert Gasser
item.description: Game 3 of the World Series brings a remarkably familiar opponent for the Milwaukee Brewers in Tampa Bay Rays starting pitcher Freddy Peralta , whose eight years in Milwaukee coincided with the best run in franchise history. The right-hander has been on a remarkable run since he was traded from the New York Mets to the Rays at the deadline, one year and 12 days since he pitched his final game for the Brewers in the National League Championship Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers . "There's a lot of emotion because those guys know each other so well, so you gotta keep that emotion under control," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said Oct. 26, hours before the Brewers tried to expand their World Series lead in the series to 3-0 against the American League Championship Series MVP Peralta. "It comes down to pitches, it comes down to you and the ball, not so much you and the pitcher. So I don't look at that as an advantage or disadvantage. "You get to do this a lot in baseball, 30 different teams, a lot of those guys play for you. My first managerial win ever in 2015 [as interim manager with the San Diego Padres], I had a 24-pack of Diet Dr. Pepper [delivered] from Eric Sogard, who played for me in college. I nicknamed him Soda Boy because he used to make sure my drink of choice gets on the bus. He was a freshman, so he was Soda Boy. He beat us the first game I ever managed. He beat us with a hit in the ninth." Sogard, who played under Murphy at Arizona State, played for another team with Murphy on staff when he joined the Brewers in 2018 and 2020. Murphy pointed out another obvious example, that close friend Craig Counsell manages his team's biggest rival, the Chicago Cubs. "You're going to have that throughout the league with so many players," Murphy said. "You just have to play baseball." Peralta had a 3.25 ERA over 10 games with the Rays in the regular season. In the playoffs, he has allowed just two earned runs in 16⅔ innings, with 12 strikeouts and seven walks, good for a 1.08 ERA. In his last 11 appearances including regular season and playoffs, he has allowed five earned runs in 50⅔ innings, good for a 0.88 ERA. Countering is Robert Gasser, who's made two strong postseason outings thus far after rolling through a promising September. In his last eight outings including playoffs, he's allowed seven earned runs in 41⅓ innings, good for a 1.52 ERA. He allowed just one earned run in nine playoff innings so far. "This year he's found himself a little bit uncertain of himself and then got a little more certain, so I think it is something that is a matter of confidence, and his confidence is in a good spot," Murphy said of Gasser. "But now you've got to execute pitches." This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: World Series Game 3 pitching matchup features Freddy Peralta vs. Robert Gasser

item.description: A picture-in-picture of Bill Simmons and Cathy Engelbert. The leadership of the WNBA has come under heavy criticism throughout the 2026 season, some of it in good faith and some of it not so much. Back in August, Bill Simmons spoke out forcefully against WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert, arguing that she should be replaced. With Engelbert retiring at the end of the calendar year, Simmons doesn’t have to worry about her holding the position for much longer. However, he could not hold back from taking another shot at Engelbert and her constituents on Monday following the scheduling announcement for Game 6 of the WNBA Finals. What to know Earlier today, the WNBA revealed how it would handle its scheduling conflict for Thursday’s Game 6: the Atlanta Dream and Golden State Valkyries would tip off at 12:30 p.m. ET from State Farm Arena in Atlanta, while the NBA’s Atlanta Hawks would push back their game, originally scheduled for 7 p.m., to 8 p.m. in order to accommodate the change. The Dream and Valkyries were originally slated to play at 8 p.m. ET, but in order to do so, would not have been able to play at the larger State Farm Arena because of the Hawks game. Gateway Center Arena, the Dream’s usual home venue, has capacity for only 3,500 fans. “The sellout crowds and extraordinary atmosphere at State Farm Arena for Games 3 and 4 were a tremendous success, and we’re excited to give thousands more fans the opportunity to experience Game 6 with a championship on the line,” Engelbert said in a press release. “We thank the NBA, Dream, Valkyries, Hawks, State Farm Arena and USA Network for the collaboration and flexibility that made this move possible. We look forward to delivering another unforgettable Finals experience in Atlanta. The early afternoon start time has been met with pushback from fans and media members alike , and it’s why Simmons took aim at Engelbert on X. ‘One of the dumbest leadership seasons’ “Incredible! A heroic finishing touch to one of the dumbest leadership seasons in professional sports history. They’ve had like 12 major decisions in 2026 and somehow went 0 for 12. People want to like this league!” The Ringer founder tweeted . In a follow-up tweet , Simmons joked that USA Network, which will broadcast Game 6, will preempt “three hours of ‘Chicago PD’ re-runs” in order to show the action. This storyline isn’t going anywhere, and no matter how positive Engelbert and the W attempted to be in their official announcement, we’d bet that the league is praying the Finals goes to a deciding Game 7 so they don’t have to have a championship decided on a Thursday afternoon. Game 5 of the WNBA Finals is tonight at 8 p.m. ET on USA Network, Peacock and CNBC. The Valkyries and Dream have split the first four games of the series.
